headline: SNOWLINE DRILLS 450m AT 1.47 g/t GOLD FROM SURFACE AT VALLEY — New Duke Target 12km Away Returns First 65.8m Discovery Hole; PFS Due Q1 2027
snippet: Snowline Gold (TSX-V: SGD) released 2026 Rogue Project results showing Valley infill hole V-26-165 at 450.2 metres of 1.47 g/t gold from surface — outperforming the resource block model — while the separate Duke target 12 km southeast returned a discovery hole of 65.8 metres at 1.03 g/t gold, confirming a second reduced intrusion-related gold system on the same property. With a Valley Pre-Feasibility Study due Q1 2027, confirming an independent gold system at Duke dramatically expands the district-scale investment case for one of Canada's largest undeveloped high-grade gold deposits.

headline: VIZSLA SILVER DELAYS PANUCO PRODUCTION BY A YEAR TO H2 2028 — Sinaloa Security Rebuild and Mexican Permit Backlog Push Back High-Grade Silver Project
snippet: Vizsla Silver (TSX-V: VZLA) has pushed back first silver production at its Panuco Mine in Sinaloa, Mexico from H2 2027 to H2 2028, citing unresolved federal environmental and land-use permits alongside the need to rebuild site security following the abduction and killing of 10 workers earlier in 2026. The delay extends the timeline at one of North America's highest-grade undeveloped silver-gold projects, with no production decision yet made despite approximately 85% of process plant equipment already ordered and 50% engineering complete.

headline: CABRAL GOLD M&I RESOURCES CLIMB 49% TO 999K OZ AT CUIÚ CUIÚ — Inferred Surges 376% to 2.5M oz; Brazil District-Scale System Nears 3.5M oz Total
snippet: Cabral Gold (TSX-V: CBR) announced a 49% increase in measured and indicated gold resources at the Cuiú Cuiú Gold Project in Brazil's Pará state to 42.5 million tonnes at 0.73 g/t for 998,800 oz M&I, while inferred resources jumped 376% to 2.5 million oz — a combined total approaching 3.5 million oz across all categories, with all six deposits open at depth. The updated resource builds on a prefeasibility study that pegged Phase 1 capital at just $37.7 million, keeping Cabral as one of the most capital-efficient path-to-production stories in South American gold exploration.

headline: McFARLANE LAKE DRILLS 163m AT 0.68 g/t GOLD AT JUBY ONTARIO — Including 11m At 2.13 g/t; Golden Lake Northwest Extension Grows Under 50K-Metre Winter Program
snippet: McFarlane Lake Mining (CSE: MLM) intersected 163 metres at 0.68 g/t gold at the Golden Lake Deposit within Ontario's Juby Gold Project, extending mineralization approximately 200 metres northwest of previously drilled areas as part of its fully funded 50,000-metre Phase 2 program with three drill rigs running through winter. A sub-interval of 11 metres at 2.13 g/t gold highlights the higher-grade core within the broader bulk-mineable system, which already hosts a 180.6 million tonne inferred resource at 0.87 g/t for 5.06 million ounces.

headline: GLOBAL LITHIUM A$333M TITAN SCHEME BOOKLET FILED WITH ASIC — Manna WA Lithium Deal Advances to Dec 22 Shareholder Vote; BDO Calls It Fair
snippet: ASIC registered the scheme booklet for Titan Australia Mining's A$333 million acquisition of Global Lithium Resources (ASX: GL1) on November 18, with shareholder dispatch scheduled for November 23 and a scheme meeting targeting December 22, subject to court approval. Independent expert BDO Australia concluded the A$1.15 per share offer is fair and reasonable for GL1's Manna Lithium Project in Western Australia, keeping a UAE-backed critical minerals group on track for mid-January 2027 implementation at a 73% premium to the pre-announcement price.

headline: URNM FALLS TO MAY 2025 LOW AT $37.76 AS U3O8 HOLDS $90 — Long-Term Uranium Price Hits Record $99/lb; Sprott Calls Gap 'Liquidity Shock Not Broken Thesis'
snippet: The Sprott Uranium Miners ETF (URNM) fell to its lowest level since May 2025 on November 16, closing at $37.76 — down approximately 23% year-to-date — while U3O8 spot prices held near $89.98/lb and TradeTech's long-term uranium price indicator reached a historic record of $99/lb, marking the most extreme divergence between uranium equities and uranium fundamentals in this cycle. Sprott has characterized the gap as a small-cap liquidity shock rather than a broken thesis: URNM has decoupled from the commodity and is trading with the broader risk-off tone in high-beta equities, while the fundamental case for new uranium supply — driven by 88 GWe of nuclear capacity under construction globally — remains intact.

headline: LITHIUM ETF LIT HITS 12-MONTH LOW, NOW 38% BELOW MAY PEAK — Rate Fears and Surplus Narrative Override Structural Battery Demand; Key Miners at Multi-Year Lows
snippet: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) hit a 12-month low of approximately $56.84 on November 16-17, completing a 38% decline from its May 2026 peak of $91.62 as elevated Treasury yields near 5.14%, a projected two-year supply surplus, and weaker short-term EV demand growth have compressed the entire lithium mining sector. The selloff has pushed Albemarle, Pilbara Minerals, and other major lithium names to multi-year lows relative to earnings — a valuation dislocation from long-term demand that institutional investors are beginning to characterize as a potential generational entry point despite the absence of near-term catalysts.

headline: CHINA'S TWO LARGEST RARE EARTH COMPANIES MORE THAN DOUBLE 9-MONTH PROFITS — Supply Controls Push Northern RE +136.6% and China RE Resources +112.4% Year-on-Year
snippet: China Northern Rare Earth Group reported net profit up 136.6% year-on-year to 3.65 billion yuan for the first nine months of 2026, while China Rare Earth Resources and Technology posted a 112.4% gain to 408.1 million yuan — driven almost entirely by Beijing's supply-discipline reforms that consolidated production quotas to two state-linked producers, down from six historically, and pushed NdPr oxide prices approximately 62% above pre-reform levels. For Western junior rare earth developers, the profit surge at China's state-controlled producers quantifies the pricing power that controlled supply creates — and reinforces the strategic premium US, EU, and Australian offtake buyers will pay for non-Chinese sources at current prices.
